body:
N-48 MEASUREMENT RESULT, PART 2 (26 Nov 2026, lead; part 1 has recovery and safety).

(c) COST: about 27 requests per artist (one list + two per album/EP/compilation, never a single); the whole library's held songs = 3,345 requests = 14 min at the gate: a one-off, then per newly held artist. FOR THE REAL ROUND: Catalogue.artist_page asks as a PERSON (interactive, 2.5 s) and answered 'could not be asked' for 18 of 18 artists: a background call (priority + deadline, as album() has) is needed; fail closed on a cut list (total above what came), a track list at the 100 limit, no releases (Zack Hemsey), an album that could not be asked; 4 sole_album songs have no home (Shinedown, Sum 41, Howie Day, Zack Hemsey) and stay held.

(d) YEAR: the discography's DATES do not give the year: Weathered 2009 (real 2001), The Invisible Band 2009 (2001), Contraband 1990-01-01 (2004 only if the placeholder is skipped); for 112 songs the earliest real date is a reissue (more than a year after the ISRC year) in 18. The ISRC's year digits (characters 6-7, the year the recording was registered; already in the track lists fetched, no new service, no PRIVACY change) give 2001, 2001, 2004: all three right; they equal the earliest real date's year in 70 of 112 and are within one year in 91; the 18 far cases are mostly reissue dates (Enema of the State ISRC 1999 vs 2018, Break Stuff 1999 vs 2008). It is the RECORDING's year, not the album's release (Muse 2005 vs 2006). So the stop-gap text 'the discography's album list can say the first year' (album_finder.choose_release, docs/18, CHANGELOG, board) is FALSE and is re-pointed.

DECISIONS TO BRING (the advisor, not the owner): (1) single_only: 27 of 32 have no album carrying them at all: may they become a single stamp when the list is complete? (2) year: write the ISRC year (wrong by one in about a fifth) or none; what cap against the catalogue's date. (3) by_share: only as agreement with the matcher's pick (recommended) or not at all.
